name: Tata Power Co. Ltd.
business_summary: Integrated Tata Group utility: generation (Mundra UMPP 4 GW imported coal, Jojobera, Maithon, hydro), renewables (6.7 GW; >9 GW targeted by Mar-27; TP Renewable), transmission & distribution (Mumbai licence, Delhi TPDDL, Odisha DISCOMs, Ajmer; TBCB lines), solar manufacturing (TP Solar, 4.3 GW cells/modules, rooftop), coal mines and shipping in Indonesia, EV charging, pumped hydro and Bhutan hydro. Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026): PAT Rs 1,401 cr (+11%, 27th straight quarter of EBITDA/PAT growth), underlying EBITDA Rs 4,249 cr (+8%), revenue Rs 19,051 cr. Net debt/underlying EBITDA 3.41x; capex Rs 6-6.5k cr/qtr. Q2 FY27 results pending (date not located). Mcap Rs 1.16 lakh cr, P/E 29.7; promoters (Tata Sons group) 46.86%.

revenue_mix.segment: Thermal + hydro generation incl. Mundra, Jojobera, Maithon (incl. coal/shipping pass-through)
revenue_mix.geography: India (Gujarat, Jharkhand, WB etc.); Indonesia coal ~5%

revenue_mix.segment: Renewables (utility, rooftop, TP Solar manufacturing, EPC)

exposures.mechanism: P/E 29.7, EV/MCap ~1.5 (net debt/underlying EBITDA 3.41x, net debt/equity 1.25x per mgmt; mcap Rs 1.16 lakh cr). Regulated Mumbai T&D, TBCB lines and 25-yr PPAs give long-duration, partly inflation-indexed cash flows; +25bp on ~10% WACC, duration ~13 => -3.3, minus offset from CERC/MERC RoE resets => -2.5. Pack: US-10y beta -0.99 per 25bp (t -1.7), consistent.

evidence.note: CFO: net debt to underlying EBITDA 3.41, net debt to equity 1.25
Mcap Rs 1,16,342 cr; P/E 29.7; borrowings Rs 76,141 cr (Mar-26)
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Consolidated borrowings Rs 76k cr (Mar-26), interest Rs 1,407 cr in Q1 FY27 vs PBT Rs 1,823 cr. Floating share ~50% (estimate): +25bp = Rs 95 cr/yr = -1.8% of PAT (TTM Rs 5.3k cr); regulated T&D recovers actual interest on normative debt; renewables fixed tariffs do not => 60% unrecovered => -1.1% x EV/MCap 1.5 x persistence 0.6 => -1.0 (funding channel only).

evidence.note: Interest Q1 FY27 Rs 1,407 cr; PBT Rs 1,823 cr
RBI hiked repo 25 bp to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026, first hike in ~4 years; stance calibrated tightening; cuts 'off the table' (Reuters, The Hindu, Business Standard headlines)

exposures.mechanism: Capex running Rs 6,000-6,500 cr/quarter (Q2 FY27, CFO) incl. 2.5 GW renewables, PSP and 2,000 km transmission, so net debt is rising (borrowings 62.9k -> 76.1k cr in FY26). +50bp on ~Rs 30k cr refinanced/new in 2 yrs = Rs 150 cr/yr = -2.9% PAT, 60% unrecovered, EV/MCap 1.5, persistence 0.5 => -1.8.

evidence.note: CFO: Q2 capex plan Rs 6,000-6,500 cr, ~half renewables; PSP accelerating; >2,000 km transmission in pipeline

exposures.mechanism: Renewables cluster (6.7 GW -> >9 GW by Mar-27; 2.5-2.7 GW to be added in FY27), rooftop (+100% revenue last year, +60-70% planned), TP Solar (4.3 GW cell/module capacity; 1 GW modules, 0.9 GW cells Q2) all depend on DCR/ALMM, ISTS waiver, PM Surya Ghar and storage mandates. +1 SSU => +20% on renewables+rooftop+manufacturing EBITDA growth for 2 yrs: renewables+solar ~35% of EBITDA (est.) => +3% value x 1.5 x ... => +4.

evidence.note: Sinha: renewables 6.7 GW now, >9 GW by FY-end; rooftop revenue ~+100%; ALMM-II continues for rooftop and utility
TP Solar produced 1 GW modules, 0.9 GW cells in Q2 FY27 (ET EnergyWorld, CNBC TV18)

exposures.mechanism: Broad anti-dumping/ALMM-III protection on cells, wafers, glass benefits TP Solar's integrated 4.3 GW cell+module capacity (module output peaked >1,000 MW/qtr; cell output still ramping) and raises domestic module prices, but raises costs of its own utility-scale EPC/rooftop (imported cells for non-DCR use). Mgmt: ALMM-II 'not a rollback', affects ~10% of DCR demand. Net +1.0.

evidence.note: Sinha: ALMM-II continues for rooftop and utility; special proviso ~10% of DCR requirement

exposures.mechanism: Indonesian coal stakes (KPC, Arutmin and BSSR minority holdings - model knowledge) and Mundra Coal & Shipping earn when seaborne prices rise; mgmt (Jul): coal prices +5-7%, coal profitability improving. Mundra UMPP supplementary PPA is cost-plus (actual coal cost, normative fixed cost, no ROE), so pass-through is neutral and part of coal-sale profit is netted in the tariff. Estimated Indonesian coal EBITDA Rs ~1,500-2,000 cr/yr: +15% price => +30% = +Rs 500 cr = +3% group EBITDA, 50% netted/taxed => +1.5% x EV/MCap 1.5 x 0.4 => +1.0. Pack empirical +1.88 (t +1.3) consistent.

evidence.note: Sinha: coal prices up 5-7%; supplementary PPA on actual coal cost with no ROE; Mundra scheduled under Section 11
Pack empirical F_COAL_INTL +1.88 per SSU, t +1.3

exposures.mechanism: Q1 FY27 power demand +8.5% (May +11%, June 9.8%); Tata Power's distribution volumes (Mumbai, Delhi, Odisha, Ajmer) grow with demand but are regulated; thermal/hydro PLF and Mundra dispatch rise. +3pp demand => +2.5% distribution/generation volumes => +1.2% EBITDA x 1.5 x 0.8 => +1.5.

evidence.note: Sinha: Q1 power demand growth ~8.5%, July 260-270 GW; delayed rains
Coal stocks critical as demand surges

exposures.mechanism: Limited merchant exposure: Jojobera/Maithon/IEL thermal largely PPA-backed, Mundra on supplementary PPA, renewables fixed-tariff. +15% spot => merchant slice (~6% of generation) +Rs 100-150 cr => +0.8% EBITDA x 1.5 x 0.5 => +0.7.

evidence.note: Mundra operating under Section 11 with SPPA billing; 3 states' approvals expected Aug-Sep

exposures.mechanism: Four DISCOMs (TPDDL Delhi, TPCODL/TPSODL/TPWODL Odisha, Mumbai franchise, Ajmer) - collection efficiency and tariff orders drive earnings (Odisha Q1 muted by three issues incl. collections/government dues). +1 SSU (reform progress, tariff true-up) => +5% distribution PAT growth and higher collections => +2.5.

evidence.note: Odisha growth muted in Q1 for three reasons; improvement expected; Delhi DISCOM Q&A

exposures.mechanism: Mumbai transmission ~Rs 10,000 cr regulated investment in 5 yrs; TBCB projects (Jalpura-Khurja, Bikaner-Neemrana by Oct 2026) and >2,000 km pipeline; +1 SSU => +10% regulated base growth => +2 after EV/MCap and persistence.

evidence.note: Sinha: Rs 10,000 cr Mumbai transmission investment over 5 yrs; Bikaner-Neemrana line by October

exposures.mechanism: PSP (Bhivpuri etc., first unit CY2029, 1,800 MW Shirwata soon), Bhutan hydro (Khorlochhu PPA with UPPCL signed), nuclear exploration and BESS add optionality; +1 SSU => 1.5x multiple support for transition pipeline ~ +3.

evidence.note: PSP commissioning from early CY2029; Khorlochhu 600 MW PPA signed with UPPCL, operational CY2030

exposures.mechanism: Offsetting USD exposures: imported solar wafers/cells and coal (pass-through at Mundra) cost more, but USD-linked Indonesian coal earnings and Mundra USD dollar-indexed cost recovery rise. Net near zero; +3% => +/-0.5% EBITDA noise. Rupee at 94.5.

evidence.note: SPPA on actual coal cost; Indonesian coal sales
Debt Rs 76,141 cr; Q1 FY27 sales Rs 19,051 cr

exposures.mechanism: Beta ~1.4 (pack); FII holding 10.1% flat, DIIs rising (18.5%); +US$5bn FPI inflow ~ +2% Nifty x 1.4 x 0.7 => +2.0.

exposures.mechanism: Hormuz disruption lifts seaborne coal (helps Indonesian coal earnings) and energy-security capex, but raises yields/inflation (negative for a 3.4x levered utility). Net ~0 with wide range.

evidence.note: Middle East conflict disrupting LNG/crude via Hormuz; Asia pivoting to coal (Wood Mackenzie 12 Oct, EnergyNow 3 Nov 2026 headlines)
Sinha/Q&A: Indonesian coal market commentary amid on-off Hormuz situation

company_links.mechanism: Tata Steel is Tata Power's largest industrial counterparty (Jamshedpur utility, captive/pumped-storage offtake discussions - Q1 call) and a fellow Tata Sons company. Pack shows Tata Power loading +4.88 per +15% iron ore (t +3.4) and +1.58 on steel (t +2.0), most plausibly through group/Tata-complex co-movement rather than any direct raw-material link. Tata group sell-offs on Tata Sons governance (Sep 2026, Rs 40,000 cr lost) hit both. w = % move in Tata Power per 1% move in Tata Steel (judgement).
